in_english.long_meaning: Alwyn is a name with Welsh origins, meaning 'noble friend' or 'friend of the nobles'. It is derived from the Old Welsh word 'alb' meaning 'noble' and 'guin' meaning 'friend'. Alwyn is also found in the New Testament (Acts 27:7), where it refers to a Roman centurion. In Christian tradition, Alwyn is associated with nobility, friendship, and loyalty. This name is also associated with Saint Alwyn, a 7th-century Welsh saint known for his piety and devotion. In modern times, Alwyn is a popular name in many Christian cultures, symbolizing friendship, nobility, and faith.
